editions.label: 13–26 July 2026
editions.editor_note: A Europe-weighted fortnight. Gulf coverage is thin this cycle: regional attention remains on Strait of Hormuz shipping conditions and war-risk premiums following the spring disruption, with no new in-window automotive policy or franchise developments meeting our verification threshold.

items.headline: EU car market up 5.7% in H1 2026 as battery-electric share reaches 20.7%
items.summary: ACEA reported 5.90 million new EU car registrations in the first half of 2026, up 5.7%. Battery-electric cars took 20.7% share against 15.6% a year earlier, hybrids 37.3% and plug-in hybrids 9.8%, while combined petrol and diesel fell to 29.7%.
items.so_what: Sets the powertrain mix our European franchises must supply into. Petrol and diesel losing eight points of share in a year is the number that reprices our stock and spec planning.

items.headline: EU tariffs cut China-built BEV share but Chinese brands keep growing
items.summary: Transport & Environment analysis found China-produced electric cars fell to 17% of the EU battery-electric market in Q1 2026 from a 22% peak, driven mainly by Tesla, BMW and Volvo reshoring output. Chinese-brand imports continued rising, and Chinese battery imports increased sharply.
items.so_what: Tariffs are redirecting where cars are built, not who sells them. Chinese-brand volume in Europe keeps growing, so our European portfolio thesis holds while landed-cost assumptions shift.

items.headline: Chinese brands take a third of Europe's plug-in hybrid market as duties near
items.summary: Local registration data showed Chinese brands at roughly a third of European plug-in hybrid deliveries in June, led by BYD, Chery and Geely. Reporting indicated the Commission is moving closer to duties on Chinese-built plug-in hybrids, pending member-state approval.
items.so_what: The PHEV gap that made Chinese hybrids cheap in Europe is closing. If duties land on a similar formula to BEVs, our European hybrid pricing resets inside two quarters.

items.headline: Commission publishes Electrification Action Plan with 46% target and V2G framework
items.summary: On 17 July the European Commission published its Electrification Action Plan alongside a proposed ETS review and a legislative proposal on network charges. It set an indicative 46% electrification target for 2040 and committed to regulatory sandboxes for vehicle-to-grid projects.
items.so_what: Signals the direction of EU charging and grid rules our European markets will operate under, and opens a vehicle-to-grid services angle adjacent to vehicle sales.

items.headline: Farizon adds SV Sport to UK electric commercial vehicle range
items.summary: Farizon Auto UK, distributed by Jameel Motors, expanded its electric commercial vehicle line-up with the launch of the SV Sport, announced in London on 16 July.
items.so_what: Widens our UK electric LCV offer into a fleet segment where our conversion and aftersales capability is the differentiator rather than the vehicle.
